items.title: Se7en
items.note: The ending is still the most ruthless thing a studio has ever let through, and nothing since has earned its darkness half as honestly. Fincher invented his entire visual grammar here, all rain and rot and things you only half see.

items.title: Fight Club
items.note: Everyone quotes it for the wrong reasons, which is sort of the joke and sort of the tragedy. Watch it again past thirty and it stops being cool and starts being sad, which is the better film.

items.title: Zodiac
items.note: A film about the case never closing, so of course it refuses to close. Probably his best, and the one people skip because there is no payoff, which is the entire point.

items.title: The Social Network
items.note: Dialogue at a hundred miles an hour and every single line lands. Aged into a documentary without changing a frame.

items.title: Gone Girl
items.note: The nastiest film ever made about marriage and it is having a great time being nasty. That mid film turn is structurally perfect.

items.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
items.note: A remake nobody asked for that turned out better than it had any right to be. Freezing, methodical, and that title sequence is its own short film.

items.title: Panic Room
items.note: One house, one night, and a camera that goes wherever it likes. Minor Fincher, but minor Fincher is still better built than most people's best.

items.title: The Game
items.note: Works completely the first time and collapses a little if you think too hard afterwards. Worth it for the ride and for Douglas slowly coming apart.

items.title: Alien 3
items.note: The studio broke it before he ever finished it, and you can see the better film underneath. The bleak monastery-in-space idea deserved a director with final cut.

items.title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
items.note: Beautiful and strangely weightless, like an award ceremony that lasts three hours. The one Fincher where the technique is doing all the feeling for you.

items.title: Mank
items.note: The black and white Gary Oldman one, and the only Fincher I would call boring. A film made for his father rather than for anybody watching.

items.title: The Killer
items.note: Two hours of a man being extremely good at a job while narrating nonsense to himself. The gap between what he says and what he does is the whole film.

items.title: Mulholland Drive
items.note: The best film ever made about wanting something so badly you rewrite reality to get it. Do not try to solve it on the first pass, just let it happen to you.

items.title: Lost Highway
items.note: A Mobius strip about guilt where the man literally becomes somebody else rather than admit what he did. That video tape sequence is the most frightening thing Lynch ever shot.

items.title: The Departed
items.note: A remake of Infernal Affairs that is louder, meaner and somehow better paced than the original. Everybody in it is lying and every scene is a rat looking for a rat.

items.title: Shutter Island
items.note: Scorsese doing full gothic horror and clearly enjoying himself. The last line is the whole film and it reframes everything you just sat through.

items.title: Reservoir Dogs
items.note: A heist film that never shows the heist, made for the price of a decent car. You can hear a whole decade of cinema starting in the opening diner scene.

items.title: Pulp Fiction
items.note: Rearranged what I thought a film was allowed to do with time. Still the high water mark for making people talking in a room more tense than a shootout.

items.title: Jackie Brown
items.note: His most patient and most adult film, and the one that will age best. Pam Grier carries an entire con on her face in the mall sequence.

items.title: Kill Bill Vol. 1
items.note: Pure style with the throttle stuck open, and the anime detour is the best part. The House of Blue Leaves fight is choreography as showing off, in the good way.

items.title: Kill Bill Vol. 2
items.note: The talking half, and the better half. Pai Mei and the Superman speech justify the whole two film gamble.

items.title: Death Proof
items.note: Half of it is people chatting in a bar and half of it is the best car stunt of the century. Lopsided on purpose, still lopsided.

items.title: Inglourious Basterds
items.note: That opening farmhouse scene is a masterclass in stretching a conversation until it snaps. Landa is the best villain he ever wrote and it is not close.

items.title: Django Unchained
items.note: A spaghetti western aimed straight at American history with no interest in being polite about it. Runs long in the last act but the dinner table scene earns the ticket.

items.title: The Hateful Eight
items.note: A locked room mystery shot in 70mm, which is a joke only he would commit to. Slow, mean, and better on a rewatch when you stop waiting for it to move.

items.title: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
items.note: A hangout film about being washed up, and then the ending arrives like a slap. The most affectionate thing he has made.

items.title: True Romance
items.note: Tarantino's script with Tony Scott's heart on top, which turns out to be the perfect trade. The Hopper and Walken scene is the best five minutes either of them ever had.

items.title: Nightcrawler
items.note: One of the few films that genuinely got under my skin and stayed there. Gyllenhaal plays a man with no inside, and the film is smart enough never to explain him.

items.title: Fargo
items.note: Everybody is polite and everybody is doomed, and the film finds that hilarious right up until it does not. Marge is the only decent person in it and she wins by simply doing her job.

items.title: Obsession
items.note: The recent one, and it commits hard to its premise. Nasty, funny in places, and it does not lose its nerve at the end.

items.title: Searching
items.note: Technically brilliant and emotionally tense, told entirely through screens without ever feeling like a gimmick. The format should not work this well and it does.

items.title: Baby Driver
items.note: Visual storytelling at the highest level, every cut married to the beat. Wright showing off and earning every second of it.

items.title: Shaun of the Dead
items.note: Wright's visual grammar arriving fully formed, with the jokes built into the cuts rather than the lines. Funnier on the fourth watch once you start noticing the setups.

items.title: Hot Fuzz
items.note: An action parody that is a better action film than the ones it parodies. The editing does more of the comedy than the script does.

items.title: The World's End
items.note: The last Cornetto and the saddest of the three, which sneaks up on you. Same visual precision, much heavier heart.

items.title: John Wick
items.note: Brilliant action, choreographed so you can actually see it, which almost nobody bothers with anymore. Thin on everything else and it does not matter.

items.title: John Wick: Chapter 2
items.note: Bigger, and the world building starts getting silly in the right way. Still the cleanest action shooting around.

items.title: John Wick: Chapter 3 - Parabellum
items.note: The horse sequence and the knife room justify the whole film. Plot is now openly an excuse and everybody involved knows it.

items.title: John Wick: Chapter 4
items.note: Three hours of set pieces and the stairs sequence alone is worth the ticket. The best looking of the four.

items.title: The Batman
items.note: Brilliant and genuinely cinematic, the best looking comic book film anybody has made. The only real problem with it is how far away the sequel still is.

items.title: Caught Stealing
items.note: Gritty production design and real ambience, it genuinely gives you the Lock Stock feeling. Aronofsky loosening up and clearly enjoying himself.

items.title: Snatch
items.note: Ritchie at his sharpest. The plot is a watch mechanism and every single part clicks into the next one, and it has not aged a day.

items.title: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
items.note: The one that started all of it, made for nothing and still funnier than anything that has tried the same trick since. You can watch the whole British crime revival begin here.

items.title: Sherlock Holmes
items.note: A perfectly good time, and Downey and Law have real chemistry. Style over substance and it never pretends otherwise.

items.title: Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows
items.note: More of the same, slightly bigger, still fun. A two and no complaints.

items.title: Memento
items.note: The structure is the story, and no one has done the trick better since. Built backwards and it still lands emotionally, which is the hard part.

items.title: The Dark Knight
items.note: Obviously. A crime film wearing a cape, and Ledger rewrote what the role could be.

items.title: Batman Begins
items.note: A solid two. Does the hard work of making the origin believable so the next one could fly.

items.title: Inception
items.note: The dream inside a dream one. Impeccably built, a bit cold, and the rules take up more room than the feeling.

items.title: Interstellar
items.note: Gorgeous and overreaching in equal measure. The docking scene and the score do most of the lifting.

items.title: Tenet
items.note: Technically astonishing and emotionally inert. You spend the whole film solving it rather than watching it.

items.title: Dunkirk
items.note: The war one. Three timelines squeezed into one long held breath, more experiment than drama.

items.title: Insomnia
items.note: Mid. Pacino and Williams are worth watching and the film around them never quite wakes up.

items.title: Oppenheimer
items.note: Not watched yet.

items.title: It Follows
items.note: Amazing, and the score is half of why. A Carpenter tribute that stands entirely on its own legs.

items.title: Let the Right One In
items.note: The Scandinavian original, and brilliant on visuals. Unsettling and genuinely beautiful about bullying and childhood at the same time.

items.title: Talk to Me
items.note: A great way to make a horror film. Slick, stylish, modern, and it never coasts on the gimmick.

items.title: Bring Her Back
items.note: The follow up, and properly unsettling. More of a two than Talk to Me but still worth your time.

items.title: Audition
items.note: Massively unsettling, and it earns it by making you wait. The first hour is a different film entirely, which is the trap.

items.title: Oldboy
items.note: Just as unsettling and just as good. The corridor fight, the ending, all of it still lands.

items.title: Hereditary
items.note: A two. Extremely well made and it never quite justifies how unpleasant it is.

items.title: Midsommar
items.note: Same as Hereditary, a two. Beautiful to look at and much too long for what it has to say.

items.title: Parasite
items.note: A two. Immaculately built and a little too pleased with the metaphor.

items.title: Memories of Murder
items.note: Good technique, low on the entertainment quotient. Zodiac is open ended too and is the better film.

items.title: Don't Breathe
items.note: A great entertainer. One house, one very bad idea, and it moves.

items.title: Don't Breathe 2
items.note: Still entertaining, just not worth the time. A one.

items.title: Sisu
items.note: Brilliant action, and worth it for the cinematography alone. Beautiful Finnish grit and almost no dialogue.

items.title: Sisu: Road to Revenge
items.note: A two rather than a three, and still shot beautifully. Same grit, slightly less surprise.

items.title: The Silence of the Lambs
items.note: Obviously a three. Thrilling and visceral, and it rewards going back again and again.

items.title: Heat
items.note: Remarkably modern for its age. Mann shooting a city at night better than anyone before or since.

items.title: Manhunter
items.note: The same remarkable modernity, and the first Lecter on screen. Cold, blue, and years ahead of itself.

items.title: The Bourne Identity
items.note: The one that reset the whole genre. Grounded, fast, and it still holds up.

items.title: The Bourne Supremacy
items.note: The middle one, and the weakest. A one.

items.title: The Bourne Ultimatum
items.note: Back up to a two and the best set pieces of the three. Waterloo station alone.

items.title: My Cousin Vinny
items.note: Immense rewatchability and a brilliant, brilliant film. Essentially a textbook on how feel good movies should be made. What a movie.

items.title: The Big Lebowski
items.note: The same immense rewatchability. Nothing happens and every scene is quotable.

items.title: Good Will Hunting
items.note: A two. Williams is genuinely great and the rest is more sentimental than it admits.

items.title: Argo
items.note: A good entertainer, not worth the time. A one.

items.title: The Vanishing
items.note: One of the truly disturbing films, and visceral in a way almost nothing else manages. The ending is the most frightening thing I have sat through and there is no violence in it at all.

items.title: The Gentlemen
items.note: Also good, and a must watch. Ritchie back on home turf after a long detour, with a cast clearly having a great time.

items.title: Incendies
items.note: Disturbing, and it does not let you off at the end. The kind of film you sit with in silence for a while afterwards.

items.title: Prisoners
items.note: A great mystery, patiently built and genuinely hard to call. Everybody in it is compromised and the film refuses to tell you who to side with.

items.title: Sicario
items.note: Brilliant for the performances and the camera work above all. Del Toro and Blunt pulling opposite directions, and Deakins shooting the border like a war zone.

items.title: Arrival
items.note: A two, and still a must watch. Science fiction that is actually about grammar and grief rather than spaceships.

items.title: Enemy
items.note: A two, not a must watch. Deliberately opaque, and the last shot is the only thing most people remember, fairly.

items.title: Iratta
items.note: Two brothers, one uniform, and a film that refuses to raise its voice even once. Malayalam cinema doing in two hours what Hindi thrillers cannot manage in three.

items.title: Titli
items.note: The most honest film about an Indian family I have seen, and it is horrifying. No score, no relief, just people trapped in a house doing damage to each other.

items.title: Ratsasan
items.note: Watch the Tamil original, the remakes all sanded off the edges. Genuinely tense, properly plotted, and it does not cheat you at the reveal.

items.title: Drishyam
items.note: The original Malayalam one, everything after is a photocopy. A perfect machine of a script where an ordinary man out-thinks the entire police force using only what he already knew.

items.title: Drishyam 2
items.note: A sequel nobody needed that justified itself completely, which almost never happens. Spends an hour on ordinary life before you realise the trap was being built the whole time.

items.title: Maharaja
items.note: The timeline trick is doing a lot of work but it works, and Vijay Sethupathi is very good at looking like a man holding something in. Wobbles in places, sticks the landing.

items.title: Thudarum
items.note: Decent. Mohanlal is excellent and the film around him is only fine, which is a fair trade for two hours.

items.title: Dhurandhar
items.note: Part one of two, and a solid two on craft. Goes big when it should go quiet, which is the standard Hindi problem.

items.title: Khosla Ka Ghosla!
items.note: Good rather than great, a Delhi middle class comedy built out of real people. Anupam Kher's small dignified fury is the best thing in it.

items.title: Oye Lucky! Lucky Oye!
items.note: A thief film that is really a class film, and it is funny enough that you barely notice. Paresh Rawal playing three men who are all the same man is the joke of the decade.

items.title: Love Sex Aur Dhokha
items.note: Made in 2010 and it predicted the next fifteen years of Indian internet culture. Formally braver than anything Bollywood has attempted since.

items.title: Shanghai
items.note: A cold, unsentimental political thriller that assumes you are paying attention. Emraan Hashmi is a genuine surprise and the ending refuses to comfort anyone.

items.title: Detective Byomkesh Bakshy!
items.note: 1940s Calcutta rendered better than the plot deserves. Overstuffed, and I still want the four sequels we never got.

items.title: Sandeep Aur Pinky Faraar
items.note: Did not land for me. Interesting on paper, a one in practice.

items.title: Black Friday
items.note: The best Indian procedural ever made and it took three years to get past the courts. That foot chase through the chawls is the single best sequence in Hindi cinema.

items.title: Gulaal
items.note: Messy, operatic, furious, and the songs are doing half the storytelling. Piyush Mishra wrote and performed his way into a film that is still underseen.

items.title: Dev.D
items.note: Genre defining and still ahead of its time. Devdas rebuilt for people who find Devdas insufferable, and Amit Trivedi's soundtrack is the actual protagonist.

items.title: Ek Hasina Thi
items.note: A lean revenge thriller with no fat on it, made before anyone knew who Raghavan was. Urmila is genuinely frightening in the back half.

items.title: Johnny Gaddaar
items.note: The purest genre film India has produced, a noir with no interest in a message. Every plan goes wrong in a way you could have predicted and never do.

items.title: Agent Vinod
items.note: The one that did not come together, though the single take Raabta sequence is worth the price alone. Ambitious in a way that failing is still interesting.

items.title: Badlapur
items.note: Technically brilliant, and a revenge film where revenge slowly turns the hero into the worse man. Nawazuddin walks off with it and the film knows it.

items.title: AndhaDhun
items.note: A black comedy thriller that keeps escalating past the point where any other film would stop. That last shot is an argument you can still have with people.

items.title: Merry Christmas
items.note: One night, two strangers, and Raghavan patiently doing his thing while everyone waits for a twist. Slower than the marketing promised and better than the reception suggested.

items.title: Animal
items.note: Technically brilliant, excelling in screenplay and editing, whatever you make of the rest of it. The craft is not the part that is in question.

items.title: Dhurandhar 2
items.note: A bit lengthy, and it spends real time whitewashing demonetisation. Still a two on craft alone.

items.title: Laapataa Ladies
items.note: A nice family friendly film, warmer than it is sharp. Pleasant, well made, and nobody gets hurt.

items.title: Bareilly Ki Barfi
items.note: A nice entertainer with a light touch and good small town texture. Does exactly what it sets out to do.

items.title: Vicky Donor
items.note: A passtime, and a good natured one. Ayushmann's debut and still one of his easiest films to sit through.

items.title: Ugly
items.note: Kashyap at his most punishing, and not in a way that earns it. A one, and I have no interest in going back.

items.title: Aamis
items.note: Super poetic, with imagery that stays with you long after. A film that could easily have been lurid and instead handles its subject with real delicacy.

items.title: Bhoothakalam
items.note: Brilliant in its performances, and in how it finds horror in ordinary daily life. The portrayal of mental health is the real subject and it is handled well.

items.title: Queen
items.note: A must watch. Kangana carries the whole thing and the film never condescends to her.

items.title: Masaan
items.note: Brilliant writing and authentic performances, with social commentary that never turns into a lecture. Quietly one of the best of its decade.

items.title: Omkara
items.note: Saif is extraordinary in it, the best thing he has done. Naseeruddin Shah has barely any screen time and is unforgettable anyway.

items.title: Laal Kaptaan
items.note: Saif is very good and the cinematography is better. A strange, dusty film that did not find its audience.

items.title: Manorama Six Feet Under
items.note: The Abhay Deol one, and a good one. Chinatown relocated to small town Rajasthan and it works better than it has any right to.

items.title: Udta Punjab
items.note: The character work is the whole film, four lives that barely touch and every one of them earned. Alia Bhatt is extraordinary in it and Shahid has never been better.

items.title: Dedh Ishqiya
items.note: Richer than the first one and more interested in its women. Madhuri and Huma play a game the men never realise they are losing, and the Urdu is a pleasure by itself.

items.title: Ishqiya
items.note: Naseeruddin Shah and Arshad Warsi are wonderful together and Vidya Balan runs rings around both. Chaubey writing adults who behave like adults, which is rarer than it should be.

items.title: Super Deluxe
items.note: Vijay Sethupathi like never before, and the whole film is that ambitious. Four stories that have no business fitting together and somehow do.

items.title: Vikram Vedha
items.note: The Tamil original, and the Hindi remake is not worth your time. A moral argument disguised as a thriller, with Sethupathi and Madhavan trading the upper hand every reel.

items.title: Vikram
items.note: A masala entertainer that knows exactly what it is doing. The action sequences and the soundtrack carry it, and the Rolex intro is the best two minutes in recent Tamil cinema.

items.title: Shor in the City
items.note: The best thing Raj and DK have made. Three stories in a city that could not care less about any of them, and it stays with you.

items.title: Go Goa Gone
items.note: Entertaining, and the first Indian zombie comedy that actually worked. Saif is having a wonderful time and it is infectious.
An early one and a good one. Small, scrappy and genuinely funny, before anybody knew who they were.

items.title: Stree
items.note: A two, and skip the sequel. Funnier and better made than the premise has any right to be.

items.title: Severance
items.note: The highest rated thing on this entire site. A perfect idea executed with total confidence, where the office satire and the existential horror are the same joke.

items.title: Furious
items.note: Not bad, kinda mid. Watchable enough to keep going, not good enough to recommend to anybody.

items.title: The Chestnut Man
items.note: Danish crime at its bleakest and most controlled, which is saying something. Trusts you to keep up rather than explaining itself every ten minutes.

items.title: Mindhunter
items.note: Two men interviewing killers in rooms, and it is tenser than any chase ever filmed. Fincher's fingerprints are all over the pacing, and cancelling it was a genuine crime.

items.title: Dept. Q
items.note: A cold case unit staffed by the people nobody else wanted, and the show is smart enough to make that the point. Properly plotted, properly acted, no filler.

items.title: Black Bird
items.note: The two lead performances are the whole thing and both are extraordinary. Hauser in particular does something genuinely unsettling with very little.

items.title: Sherlock
items.note: The technical transitions and the visual storytelling are what make it, not the plots. Text on screen, cuts inside a thought, beautiful imagery doing work that dialogue would have ruined.

items.title: Better Call Saul
items.note: Better than Breaking Bad on character work and it is not close. Subtler, slower, and it trusts you to notice things instead of pointing at them.

items.title: Breaking Bad
items.note: Great, but a bit masala, a bit in your face, everything underlined twice in case you missed it. A two next to what came after it.

items.title: Pluribus
items.note: Interesting concept and great filming, but super slow and it does not come together crisply. Skip it if you want, I would not argue.

items.title: The Office (UK)
items.note: Twelve episodes and a special, then it stopped, which is the most British thing about it. Bleaker and more uncomfortable than the American one ever tried to be.

items.title: The Office (US)
items.note: Takes a season to find itself and then becomes the most rewatchable thing on television. Warmer than the original and better for it.

items.title: Parks and Recreation
items.note: The most generous comedy ever made, where the joke is never cruelty. Leslie Knope is the only fictional character I would actually vote for.

items.title: Seinfeld
items.note: The show about nothing that is actually about how awful everyone is. Thirty years on and the plotting is still tighter than anything current.

items.title: Arrested Development
items.note: Every joke is planted three episodes early and pays off once you have forgotten it. Denser than anything else in the genre.

items.title: The Lincoln Lawyer
items.note: A great passtime when you are multitasking, which is exactly the right use for it. Nothing demanded of you and nothing wasted either.

items.title: The Penguin
items.note: Great character development, which is not what anybody expected from a Batman spinoff. Farrell disappears completely and Milioti walks off with the back half.

items.title: The Gentlemen
items.note: Ritchie doing Ritchie at series length and it holds across all eight. Sharp, funny, and cast perfectly down to the smallest part.

items.title: MobLand
items.note: Entertaining, and it knows exactly what it is. Hardy and Brosnan circling each other for ten hours is a perfectly good reason to watch anything.

items.title: The Day of the Jackal
items.note: Redmayne is the whole reason to watch and he is genuinely excellent, cold and precise and never once showing you the inside. The show around him is solid rather than special.

items.title: Daredevil
items.note: The action sequences and the camera work are what set it apart, that corridor fight above all. Shot like a film back when nobody else on streaming was bothering.

items.title: The Bureau
items.note: It ropes you in emotionally and does not let go. The character work is exceptional and the depiction of the trade is as close to authentic as the genre gets.

items.title: Broadchurch
items.note: A two. The first season is the one, and the town does as much work as the case.

items.title: Bodyguard
items.note: A mass entertainer with great performances. A two, and it knows exactly what it is.

items.title: Tehran
items.note: The performances carry it, and the sense of place is genuinely good. Tense without needing to shout.

items.title: Sacred Games
items.note: A two, and still a must watch for what it was. India's first real foray onto the global stage in the Netflix series format.

items.title: Asur
items.note: It has its flaws and it is brilliantly put together anyway. A thriller that will not stop entertaining you, and you will want to binge it.

items.title: Paatal Lok
items.note: Gritty in a way Indian television usually is not. A two and a must watch.

items.title: Decoupled
items.note: A good one, and still a must watch. Madhavan playing a man nobody should like and getting away with it.

items.title: The Ba***ds of Bollywood
items.note: A masala entertainer and perfectly happy being one. A two.

items.title: Scam 1992
items.note: The lead performance and the technical work are both excellent. A solid two, not a must watch.

items.title: Mirzapur
items.note: Has some good bits and is not worth the time. A one.

items.title: Tanaav
items.note: Decent work adapting Fauda and it does not live up to the potential. A one.

items.title: The Family Man
items.note: A must watch, and the first season especially. A spy show where the hardest part of the job is getting home in time for dinner.

items.title: Farzi
items.note: More of an entertainer than anything else. Sethupathi and Shahid are good value and the show never digs much deeper than that.

items.title: Guns & Gulaabs
items.note: Has its moments and is skippable. The tone wobbles and the length does it no favours.

items.title: Citadel: Honey Bunny
items.note: Not much to highlight or remember. A one.

items.title: Your Erroneous Zones
items.note: Currently reading. The famous one, and so far it is blunter than the modern self-help shelf, which is probably why it lasted.

items.title: Meditations
items.note: A man writing notes to himself with no idea anyone would read them, which is exactly why it works. Reads like advice from someone too tired to lie to you.

items.title: The Laws of Human Nature
items.note: The same great description of human nature, at more length and with more patience. Greene is very good at this.

items.title: Ego Is the Enemy
items.note: Stoicism repackaged for people who will not read Aurelius directly, and there is no shame in that. Says one thing well and then says it forty more times.

items.title: The 48 Laws of Power
items.note: A great description of human nature, which is what it is actually for. Read it as observation, not as instruction.

items.title: Fooled by Randomness
items.note: On the shelf. The one everybody says is the best Taleb before he started writing mainly about his enemies.

items.title: Skin in the Game
items.note: On the shelf. One good idea that reportedly justifies the whole book, assuming you can tolerate the delivery.

items.title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing
items.note: On the shelf. Everyone says the entire argument fits on a postcard, which is a point in its favour.

items.title: Healing Back Pain
items.note: On the shelf. The origin point for the whole mind-body pain literature that half my shelf now belongs to.

items.title: The Body Keeps the Score
items.note: On the shelf. The one everybody has recommended to me and nobody has finished.

items.title: Unlearn Your Pain
items.note: On the shelf. More workbook than book, which probably means it only works if you actually do it.

items.title: The Way Out
items.note: On the shelf. The most recent attempt at the Sarno idea with actual trial data behind it.

items.title: Option B
items.note: On the shelf. Grief plus research, which could go either very well or very badly.

items.title: No Rules Rules
items.note: On the shelf. Netflix explaining Netflix, so grade the whole thing on a curve.

items.title: The Tipping Point
items.note: On the shelf. The one that created the entire genre, for better and mostly for worse.

items.title: Blink
items.note: On the shelf. Snap judgement as a superpower, from before the replication crisis had opinions about that.

items.title: Outliers
items.note: On the shelf. Famous for one number that turned out to be mostly wrong, which is very Gladwell.

items.title: David and Goliath
items.note: On the shelf. Underdogs, reframed, at length.

items.title: Talking to Strangers
items.note: On the shelf. Reportedly his most serious and least fun, which might be the right direction.

items.title: The Beginning of Infinity
items.note: On the shelf. The one book on this list that people describe as actually changing how they think, so it keeps getting postponed.

items.title: Essays and Aphorisms
items.note: On the shelf. Professional pessimism, elegantly done, in small enough pieces to survive.

items.title: Assimil: French With Ease
items.note: On the shelf, in progress in theory. The method only works if you show up daily, which is the whole problem.

items.title: In Cold Blood
items.note: An absolute masterpiece and the book that invented an entire form. Capote makes you understand the killers without once asking you to forgive them.

items.title: Three Men in a Boat
items.note: A book from 1889 that is still genuinely funny, which almost nothing manages. Nothing happens, slowly, and it is delightful.

items.title: Lamb to the Slaughter
items.note: The perfect short story and the perfect last line. Everything Dahl learned about cruelty in ten pages.

items.title: Collected Short Stories
items.note: Read nearly all of them and would happily start again. Cruel, immaculate, and never a wasted sentence. The Open Window and Sredni Vashtar first.

items.title: The Complete Short Stories
items.note: The master of the ending you did not see and should have. Formula after a while, but what a formula.

items.title: The Night We Won the Buick
items.note: A poor family wins a Buick in a raffle and the father realises the winning ticket is his boss's. Stuck with me for the decision at the centre of it rather than for the writing.
items.flag: the blog you linked carries no author credit, so this is still unattributed

items.title: Collected Poems
items.note: Read nearly all of it. Half of it is a man complaining and the other half is the plainest honest writing anyone has managed about being broke and alive.

items.title: The Fountainhead
items.note: Read it in college, which is the correct and possibly only time to read it. Compelling for about four hundred pages and then it starts lecturing.

items.title: Atlas Shrugged
items.note: The other college one. There is a sixty page speech in it and that tells you most of what you need to know.

items.title: Gunda
items.note: One of the great Hindi short stories and a definite must read. A thug given a moment of real dignity, written without a shred of sentimentality.

items.title: Poos Ki Raat
items.note: A farmer, a cold night, and a small surrender that lands like a gut punch. Premchand doing more with a blanket and a field than most novels manage in four hundred pages.

items.title: Namak Ka Daroga
items.note: Honesty costs the man everything and the story is clear eyed enough to admit that. A two, and still one I go back to.

items.title: Khudai Fojdar
items.note: The other of my two favourites. Funny and sharp and quietly furious about the same things he was always furious about.

items.title: Godan
items.note: The great Hindi novel of rural debt and it never once tips into melodrama. Hori wanting one cow is the whole tragedy of a system in a single want.

items.title: Collected Short Stories
items.note: Read nearly all of them and would say the short stories are where he is strongest. Realism with no interest in making you comfortable.

items.title: Midnight's Children
items.note: A must read. History and hallucination sharing one nose, and it earns every trick it pulls.

items.title: Shame
items.note: The other must read Rushdie, meaner and tighter than Midnight's Children. A country rewritten as a family that cannot stop humiliating itself.

items.title: The God of Small Things
items.note: The prose does things English is not supposed to allow. Tells you the ending early and it still destroys you when it arrives.

items.title: The White Tiger
items.note: A nasty, fast, very funny book about getting out by any means. Thinner than its reputation but it goes down in two sittings.

items.title: Cry, the Peacock
items.note: A must read. All interior, all pressure, a mind coming apart in slow motion with nobody around noticing.

items.title: Annihilation of Caste
items.note: A must read, and the single clearest piece of argument written in modern India. A speech so unanswerable they cancelled the event rather than hear it.

items.title: The Gene: An Intimate History
items.note: Science writing that remembers it is also a family story. Long, and it earns most of the length.

items.title: India After Gandhi
items.note: On the shelf. The standard account of the republic, and it is a brick.

items.title: The Ocean of Churn
items.note: On the shelf. History told from the water rather than the capital, which is a good idea for a book.

items.title: Land of the Seven Rivers
items.note: On the shelf. Indian history through its rivers and its geography.

items.title: Atmamun
items.note: On the shelf. Very short, apparently very blunt, and unusually hostile to its own genre.

items.title: Ashtavakra Gita
items.note: On the shelf, in translation. The one that skips the practice and just states the conclusion.

items.title: The Book of Life
items.note: On the shelf. A daily reader, so it is designed to be picked at rather than finished.
